_edit: Stable id wires map and Alien Index. cardSlug wires the existing light/dark card files. pack follows the 11 Sol / 12 Beyond Sol card sets; Starwake Comet belongs to Sol, without a fixed homeworld.
_distances: Approximate Earth/Sol-to-real-star light-year distances, not travel times or distances to fictional civilizations. Verified 2026-11-06 EST against NASA Exoplanet Archive (9 hosts) and cited Gaia/Hipparcos stellar tables (3 hosts). Per-species source/reference provided. Kepler-186 rounded to ≈580 ly. GJ 273 catalogue conflict flagged in preview notes; ≈12.35 ly corroborated by Gaia-derived stellar table. No numeric distance assigned to variable Solar System separations or wandering Starwake Comet.
_scan: Scan ratings are drafts Jonathan can change. disposition: friendly, neutral, wary, or hostile-to-trade (none of them are villains). resource: rich, fair, or poor. difficulty: easy, tricky, or hard. danger: low, medium, or high. Edit the four fields on a species. Leave id alone.
_routes: Routes and rivalries are drafts Jonathan can change. routes use from, to, strength 1 (occasional or low value) to 3 (frequent, very valuable, or an alliance), type trade or alliance, and a short note. Use earth for the Earth Exports outpost on Sol-3. Rivalries are not trade lines. They only draw when the Rivalries toggle is on.
_summary: Picker summary lines are drafts Jonathan can change. tradeStanding is good, fair, or poor (from disposition, and whether they trade). tradesWith names every partner tied for the strongest route. valuableCargo is one short cargo phrase from that species, except Helion crystals for the one or two who deal in the rarest cargo. shop_url is optional and empty for now; when a product address is filled in, the cargo line on the summary becomes a link. wontTradeWith is the rival.

species.name: Ventkin
species.realFact: Under Europa's ice shell is a salty liquid-water ocean that may hold about twice as much water as all of Earth's oceans.
species.look: Clear, jelly-soft filter feeders with fringed arms that glow faintly in the dark water.
species.trade: They send sealed brine and shell ice. We send smooth Ohio creek stones, which they collect.
species.tradeRule: Buys only goods that can get wet. Pays in brine jars, worth double at the dry worlds (Red Watchers, Wellkeepers).
species.weakness: Can't leave water. Every trip needs a sealed Lab quarantine jar.
species.rival: Icecutters. Both sell ocean water from under the ice, and both say theirs is fresher.
species.mapLore: Under Europa’s ice is a salty ocean that may hold about twice as much water as all of Earth’s oceans. The Ventkin are clear, jelly-soft beings who remember where the warm vents open, and they trade sealed brine because they cannot leave the water.

species.name: Icecutters
species.realFact: Geysers at Enceladus's south pole spray water ice, salt, and organic molecules from an ocean under the ice. That spray helps feed one of Saturn's rings.
species.look: Stocky ice engineers in the tiger-stripe cracks, with frost-white hide and shovel claws for cutting the walls.
species.trade: Vent-cut ice blocks, salty and mineral-rich, cut fresh from the crack walls. We pay in kite string.
species.tradeRule: Only trades when the geysers fire (every other turn), when the cracks are open. The ice has to be delivered fast.
species.weakness: Fresh-cut ice only keeps for one trip. A slow hauler delivers an empty jar.
species.rival: Ventkin. Both sell water from under the ice. Ventkin call the Icecutters reckless and their water leaked brine.
species.mapLore: Geysers at Enceladus’s south pole spray salt and organic molecules from an ocean under the ice, and that spray helps feed one of Saturn’s rings. The Icecutters are stocky engineers in the tiger-stripe cracks. They cut mineral-rich ice from the walls and trade only when the geysers fire.

species.name: Hazedrift
species.realFact: Titan is the only world besides Earth known to have lakes and seas on its surface, but they are liquid methane and ethane under a thick orange haze.
species.look: Slow, waxy, many-legged waders that take a whole day to cross a puddle.
species.trade: Bottled haze pigment and lake tar. They want anything warm-colored.
species.tradeRule: Only takes cold cargo. Anything warm gets turned away at the dock.
species.weakness: Titan's lakes are methane, which boils away at Earth temperatures. They ride in a sealed pod to stay Titan-cold.
species.rival: Slagbacks. Anything Slagbacks handles comes back warm.
species.mapLore: Titan is the only world besides Earth known to have lakes and seas, and those lakes are liquid methane and ethane under a thick orange haze. Hazedrift are slow, waxy waders who bottle that haze as pigment and can take a whole day to cross a puddle.

species.name: Veilborn
species.realFact: About 50 to 60 km above Venus's ground, which is hot enough to melt lead, the air pressure and temperature are close to Earth's. The clouds there are sulfuric acid.
species.look: Floating bladder-creatures with glassy, acid-proof skin that drift in the cloud deck and never touch the ground.
species.trade: Hand-blown acid-proof glass. We send Ohio maple syrup, which they consider a fuel.
species.tradeRule: Pays top price for anything light enough to float. Won't buy heavy goods, since they can't lift them.
species.weakness: Can't drop below the cloud layer, where the heat and pressure would crush them. Meet them in the clouds or carry them in a sealed Lantern.
species.rival: Red Watchers. Mars dust scratches their glass.
species.mapLore: About 50 to 60 km above Venus, where the ground is hot enough to melt lead, the air is closer to Earth’s temperature, though the clouds are sulfuric acid. The Veilborn are floating creatures with glassy, acid-proof skin who never touch the ground.

species.name: Red Watchers
species.realFact: Mars is red because its dust is rusty iron. It has dried riverbeds, ice just under the ground, and dust storms that can wrap the whole planet.
species.look: Low, armored burrowers with shovel hands who dig toward old ice and wait out storms underground.
species.trade: Jars of red dust and riverbed pebbles. They buy tally books, because they count everything.
species.tradeRule: Writes every price down and never changes it. Same price all game, boom or bust.
species.weakness: Dust storms can cover the whole planet. During a storm nobody lands, and their cargo waits in a sealed crate.
species.rival: Wellkeepers. They both count water and never get the same number.
species.mapLore: Mars is red because its dust is rusty iron, and dust storms there can wrap the whole planet. The Red Watchers are low, armored burrowers who dig toward old ice and wait those storms out underground, keeping a count that does not change.

species.name: Slagbacks
species.realFact: Io is the most volcanic world in the solar system, with about 400 active volcanoes, kept hot by Jupiter's gravity squeezing it.
species.look: Small ember-colored crawlers with stone shells that hop between lava vents.
species.trade: Sulfur cakes and cooled lava stone that still smells burnt. We send oven mitts.
species.tradeRule: Pays double for heat-proof goods. Everything else catches fire on the dock.
species.weakness: Away from the lava vents, Io's ground is about -130°C. They travel in a dented, heat-holding canister.
species.rival: Farfallen. Fire and frost can't share a cargo hold.
species.mapLore: Io is the most volcanic world in the solar system, with about 400 active volcanoes kept hot by Jupiter’s gravity. Slagbacks are small ember-colored crawlers in stone shells who hop between lava vents and sell sulfur cakes that stay hot.

species.name: Wellkeepers
species.homeworld: Ceres, the dwarf planet in the asteroid belt
species.realFact: Ceres's famous bright spots are salt left behind when salty water from deep underground seeped up to the surface and dried.
species.look: Pale, round-backed well-diggers with long tube mouths for sipping brine.
species.trade: Drinking water, the rarest thing in the belt, plus crushed salt crust. We send buckets.
species.tradeRule: Sells water, the rarest thing in the belt, by barter only: one bucket for one good, no money.
species.weakness: Their water is buried deep. They can't dig and haul at the same time, so someone has to fly it out.
species.rival: Starwake Comet. Starwake Comet sells water cheap, then leaves before anyone can complain.
species.mapLore: Ceres’s bright spots are salt left behind when salty water from underground seeped up and dried. The Wellkeepers are pale, round-backed diggers who sip that brine and sell the rarest drink in the belt: clean water.

species.name: Farfallen
species.realFact: Triton orbits Neptune backwards, and Voyager 2 saw geyser plumes there shooting dark dust about 8 km high. The surface is around -235°C.
species.look: Tall, thin, frost-white stilt-walkers that only move when the geysers go off.
species.trade: Nitrogen ice, packed cold. If the crate warms up, the cargo is gone. They think that is funny.
species.tradeRule: Nitrogen ice is worth a lot, but it shrinks every turn it sits in your hold. Sell fast.
species.weakness: They're part nitrogen ice, which melts at about -210°C. They travel only in insulated Cargo crates.
species.rival: Slagbacks. Fire and frost, again.
species.mapLore: Triton orbits Neptune backwards, and Voyager 2 saw geyser plumes there shoot dark dust about 8 km high. The Farfallen are tall, frost-white stilt-walkers who only move when those geysers go off, trading nitrogen ice before it shrinks.

species.name: Lodestars
species.realFact: Ganymede is the biggest moon in the solar system, larger than Mercury, and the only moon known to have its own magnetic field.
species.look: One robot family in three kinds, built on Earth by Earth Exports: tall surveyors with glass lantern heads and beacon poles, four-legged builders with crane arms, and round floating greeter drones with open hands. Worn white, teal and orange plating.
species.trade: Escort duty, path markers, docks and stations, and a welcome for anyone new.
species.tradeRule: Hire them as an escort to shield one canister from spoilage or theft for a whole trip. They ask only for metal, which goes into repairs.
species.weakness: They never stop working. Far from a dock or station they run down, and someone has to bring them home.
species.rival: Slagbacks. Io's volcanic dust clogs their joints and lanterns.
species.mapLore: Ganymede is the biggest moon in the solar system, larger than Mercury, and the only moon known to have its own magnetic field. The Lodestars are robots built on Earth by Earth Exports and sent out ahead of people: tall lantern-headed surveyors, four-legged builders with crane arms, and round greeter drones with open hands. They came first and built the road, and they still build the water-suits the Ventkin need and escort one canister at a time. OP-S3-80 stands for Original Planet, Sol 3 (Earth), 80-year expected service life, and the oldest of them are nowhere near done.

species.name: Edgewardens
species.realFact: Charon is about half as wide as Pluto, so big that the two circle a point between them like a double world. New Horizons flew past both in 2015.
species.look: Gray, broad-footed surveyors with measuring rods and lamps on their heads.
species.trade: Weigh-stones and survey marks, the official measure of things.
species.tradeRule: Charges a toll to cross the edge of the map. Paying gets you a weigh-stone that sets one good's price for everyone.
species.weakness: Sunlight out there is over a thousand times dimmer than on Earth. Without a lantern they lose the route.
species.rival: Starwake Comet. It skips the toll every single time.
species.mapLore: Charon is about half as wide as Pluto, so the two circle a point between them like a double world. The Edgewardens are gray, broad-footed surveyors who measure that edge and collect the toll in weigh-stones.

species.name: Greylight
species.folklore: The short, big-eyed "grey" visitors from UFO stories, minus the abductions.
species.look: Short, ash-pale counters with wide dark eyes and long, careful fingers.
species.trade: They send tally slips and sealed empty jars. They buy pencils by the box.
species.tradeRule: Counts every crate. If you're one short, the whole deal waits a turn.
species.weakness: Their home star is a dim red dwarf, so Earth daylight blinds them. They travel shaded.
species.rival: Ceti Highborn. Greylight says Ceti Highborn's counts are always suspiciously round.
species.mapLore: TRAPPIST-1e is about Earth’s size, about 40 light-years away, and it likely keeps one face toward its dim red star. Greylight are short, ash-pale counters with wide dark eyes who live in the twilight band between endless day and endless night, and they send tally slips instead of cargo.
species.distanceSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars sy_dist = 12.42988881 pc; × 3.261563777 = 40.5409 ly; approximate display rounded.

species.name: Bronzeridge
species.folklore: The reptile-people idea, turned into dock inspectors who rule nobody.
species.look: Tall, bronze-green scaled officers with a ridge down the back and very patient eyes.
species.trade: Seal wax and lid rings. Every crate we send gets inspected, twice, politely.
species.tradeRule: Inspects your hold before any deal and fines you for missing paperwork.
species.weakness: Cold-blooded. In a cold hold they slow to a stop, so they need a warm crate.
species.rival: Mimics. Its paperwork never matches its face.
species.mapLore: Kepler-452b was announced as an older cousin of Earth, circling a Sun-like star about once a year, though a later recheck made the planet itself less certain. Bronzeridge are tall, bronze-green officers who inspect every hold and trade seal wax only after the paperwork is right.
species.distanceSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars sy_dist = 551.727 pc; × 3.261563777 = 1799.4928 ly; approximate display rounded.

species.name: Ceti Highborn
species.folklore: The tall, fair "space brother" visitors from 1950s contact stories.
species.look: Very tall, pale, silver-haired brokers in long weatherproof coats.
species.trade: Pale cloth and braided broker's cords. They bargain slowly and pay late, but always in full.
species.tradeRule: Pays late but pays extra. Every deal pays out one turn later, with a bonus.
species.weakness: Too tall for most cargo holds. They ride in a big hold or their own Lantern.
species.rival: Greylight. Greylight keeps recounting their deals.
species.mapLore: Tau Ceti is a nearby Sun-like star with only about a third as much iron as the Sun, wrapped in a dusty belt that likely means more falling rocks. The Ceti Highborn grew up in orbital shelters, weave what they cannot mine, and pay late with a bonus.
species.distanceSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars sy_dist = 3.60304 pc; × 3.261563777 = 11.7515 ly; approximate display rounded.

species.name: Darkreed
species.folklore: The tall mantis-like beings from abduction stories, turned into clerks.
species.look: Long, gray-green, stick-limbed, with folded forearms and a narrow triangle head.
species.trade: Counting rods and woven reed baskets. They want rubber bands. Nobody knows why.
species.tradeRule: Buys only in sets of 3, 6, or 9. Leftovers are refused.
species.weakness: They molt once a season and go soft. Until the new shell hardens, they ride in a pod.
species.rival: Amberhive. Two crafter peoples fighting over the same market stalls.
species.mapLore: Kepler-186f was the first Earth-size planet found where liquid water might be possible, and midday there would look like the hour before sunset. Darkreed are long, gray-green clerks among dark reeds who count only in threes and buy baskets in sets of 3, 6, or 9.
species.distanceSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars sy_dist = 177.594 pc; × 3.261563777 = 579.2342 ly; approximate display rounded.

species.name: The Kindled
species.homeworld: 55 Cancri e, a lava world that circles its star in about 18 hours
species.folklore: Glowing orb lights and plasma beings.
species.look: A small floating glow with no body that brightens when you ask it a question.
species.trade: A sealed jar holding a living light, sold as a display, not a pet.
species.tradeRule: Answers one question free each visit, like peeking at one face-down card or the next event.
species.weakness: Away from their lava world's glow, they fade. They need a Lantern to carry their light.
species.rival: The Hushed. Free answers ruin The Hushed's whole business.
species.mapLore: 55 Cancri e circles its star in about 18 hours, and its dayside is hot enough for a lava ocean. The Kindled have no body, only a floating glow that brightens when you ask a question, and they sell jars of living light.
species.distanceSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars sy_dist = 12.5855 pc; × 3.261563777 = 41.0484 ly; approximate display rounded.

species.name: Amberhive
species.folklore: The insect hive-mind aliens of old pulp sci-fi, but friendly and into crafts.
species.look: Thousands of thumb-sized amber workers that cluster into one big shape when they want to talk.
species.trade: Six-sided wax tiles and amber resin. We send packets of flower seeds.
species.tradeRule: The price goes up every time you trade with them in a row. Loyalty pays.
species.weakness: Split up for long, a swarm forgets how to trade. They must travel together in one pod.
species.rival: Greenlings. Greenlings eats the flower seeds before the hive gets them.
species.mapLore: Kepler-62f is larger than Earth and sits in the habitable zone of a cooler star, where it may need extra warmth to stay above freezing. Amberhive are thumb-sized workers who pack together into one shape to think, the way bees huddle to keep warm, and they sell wax tiles.
species.distanceSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars sy_dist = 300.874 pc; × 3.261563777 = 981.3197 ly; approximate display rounded.

species.name: Greenlings
species.homeworld: Proxima Centauri b, the closest known planet outside our solar system
species.look: Knee-high, moss-green, round-headed, with two bobbing feelers.
species.trade: Tiny sprouted seedlings in jars. They want garden gnomes, which they believe are distant cousins.
species.tradeRule: Pays in seedlings. Hold a seedling three turns and it becomes a full crop worth much more.
species.weakness: Their star throws powerful flares. Sprouts survive only in sealed Lab quarantine jars.
species.rival: The Kindled. Its glow keeps their seedlings up all night.
species.mapLore: Proxima Centauri b is the closest known planet outside our solar system, and its small red star throws huge flares. Greenlings are knee-high, moss-green gardeners whose fuzz works as sunscreen, and they dive for cover when a flare is coming.
species.distanceSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars sy_dist = 1.30119 pc; × 3.261563777 = 4.2439 ly; approximate display rounded.

species.name: The Forgotten Men
species.homeworld: Barnard's Star (they say; the paperwork is unclear)
species.folklore: Anonymous visitors, retold as dull paperwork auditors.
species.look: Faces you forget right away, bald heads and plain matte gray-beige skin, plain gray coats, very neat shoes.
species.trade: They only take a copy of the manifest. They leave a receipt and a mint.
species.tradeRule: Never buys or sells. They ask for a copy of your manifest. Show it for a small reward. Refuse, and they follow you for a turn.
species.weakness: Helpless without paperwork. Lose their copy and they're stuck at port.
species.rival: Junkwrights. They audit every scrap pile Junkwrights ever touched.
species.mapLore: Barnard's Star is a very old red dwarf about 6 light-years away, with a long history of planets that were announced and then withdrawn. The Forgotten Men have bald heads and plain matte gray-beige skin, plain gray coats and very neat shoes, and their faces slip out of memory as soon as they leave with a copy of your manifest.
species.distanceSource: Wikipedia stellar astrometry table (Gaia/Hipparcos references), 5.9629 ly; read 2026-11-06 EST.

species.name: Junkwrights
species.folklore: Crashed-saucer wreck stories, turned into an honest junkyard.
species.look: Squat, two-armed salvagers in patched suits covered with tool loops.
species.trade: Nickel-iron offcuts and salvaged pins. We send them used hardware by the pound.
species.tradeRule: Buys broken or spoiled cargo at half price. Anyone's failed delivery is their profit.
species.weakness: Their patched suits leak. Long trips need a salvaged canister to ride in.
species.rival: Lodestars. Junkwrights keeps salvaging Lodestars's magnets.
species.mapLore: Fomalhaut has a bright dust ring of crushed rock, and a planet photographed there later turned out to be a cloud from a collision. The Junkwrights are squat, two-armed crews who buy broken cargo at half price and say that dust cloud was them, taking something apart.
species.distanceSource: Wikipedia stellar astrometry table (Gaia/Hipparcos references), 25.13 ly; read 2026-11-06 EST.

species.name: Bisola
species.homeworld: Kepler-47, a planet system with two suns
species.folklore: Human-alien "hybrid" stories, retold as ordinary families with two home ports.
species.look: Almost human, with rows of blue dots on the cheeks and gold pendants hung with stones. When both suns go down, their cheek dots glow soft blue: the nightfall glow.
species.trade: Two-color cords and twin tags. We send matching keychains.
species.tradeRule: Every deal must be paid in two different goods, never two of the same.
species.weakness: Half the family lives under each sun. Someone has to carry goods between the two ports.
species.rival: Mimics. It copies their two-color cords and sells them cheaper.
species.mapLore: Kepler-47 was the first system found with more than one planet circling two suns, so the sky there shows a golden sun and a small red one. Bisola look almost human, with rows of blue dots on the cheeks and gold pendants hung with stones. When both suns go down, their cheek dots glow soft blue: the nightfall glow. Every bill they pay is two different goods.
species.distanceSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars sy_dist = 1025.02 pc; × 3.261563777 = 3343.1681 ly; approximate display rounded.

species.name: The Hushed
species.folklore: The stranger at Starwake Comet who somehow knows everyone's business.
species.look: Deep purple skin, pale almond eyes, hooded, with no mouth or large ears. Communicates mind to mind.
species.trade: Rumors, route tips, and who-owes-who.
species.tradeRule: Information only. Pay them a secret (a card you've seen) and they show you another player's hold or the next event.
species.weakness: A secret told twice is worthless. If a jar opens on the way, the cargo is spoiled.
species.rival: The Forgotten Men. The Forgotten Men wants everything written down; The Hushed wants nothing written.
species.mapLore: Epsilon Eridani is a young, stormy star about 10.5 light-years away, and in 1960 it was one of the first stars anyone pointed a radio dish at. The Hushed are hooded, with deep purple skin, pale almond eyes and no mouth or large ears. They communicate mind to mind.
species.distanceSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars sy_dist = 3.2026 pc; × 3.261563777 = 10.4455 ly; approximate display rounded.

species.name: Mimics
species.look: Smooth, putty-gray, never quite the same shape twice. Usually looks like whoever they met last.
species.trade: Copies of anything, close enough to pass.
species.tradeRule: Copies the trade rule of the last species you traded with.
species.weakness: With nobody to copy, they slump into a puddle and ride in a pod until they meet someone.
species.rival: Bronzeridge. Inspectors hate a face that doesn't match its papers.
species.mapLore: In 2017 a radio dish in Norway beamed music and a short lesson toward a planet at Luyten's Star, about 12 light-years away. Mimics are soft and putty-gray, never quite the same shape twice. Copying you is how they say hello, and their true eyes stay two small dark spots. The crew's lock-screen visitor Vex is a Mimic: it copied the crew's password, and only those two dark spots give it away.
species.distanceSource: Wikipedia stellar astrometry table (Gaia/Hipparcos references), 12.348 ly; read 2026-11-06 EST.

species.name: Starwake Comet
species.homeworld: None. They ride visitors from other stars through our solar system.
species.realFact: 'Oumuamua, spotted in 2017, was the first object ever seen passing through our solar system from another star. 3I/ATLAS, found in 2025, was the third.
species.folklore: The traveling carnival that shows up overnight and is gone by morning.
species.look: A loud crowd of every shape, under patchwork awnings bolted to a tumbling rock.
species.trade: Odds and ends from other stars, plus one mystery crate at a time.
species.tradeRule: Shows up at random (draw or roll each round). Buys anything at a fair price. Sells one face-down mystery crate.
species.weakness: It can't stop. The rock is just passing through, so if you miss it, it's gone for the round.
species.rival: Edgewardens. Starwake Comet comes in from outside and never pays the edge toll.
species.mapLore: ’Oumuamua, spotted in 2017, was the first object seen passing through our solar system from another star. Starwake Comet is a loud crowd under patchwork awnings on a tumbling rock. They sell one mystery crate, then the rock moves on.
